I'm 60 years old and I've been farming these 9 mu in Quzhou for over 35 years. With my high school education, I understand the technical side better than some of my neighbors, but experience is what I trust most. This year I'll stick with my proven system: 5 mu of wheat-maize double cropping and 4 mu of cotton. The wheat-maize rotation is my insurance policy—even if cotton prices drop or bollworm hits hard, I still have grain to sell and eat. I planted Jimai 22 wheat last October; it's a reliable improved variety that gives me around 1000 kg per mu when managed well. For fertilizer, I'm targeting 20 kg of nitrogen per mu for wheat, split between basal dressing and jointing-stage topdress, plus 8 kg phosphorus and 6 kg potassium. I know some farmers cut back on fertilizer to save money, but at my age I've learned that skimping on inputs costs more in lost yield than it saves in cash. I'll irrigate the wheat four times—the groundwater pumping is expensive but necessary in our dry springs. For summer maize, I'll plant Denghai 605 hybrid right after wheat harvest in mid-June. There's no time for tillage between crops, so I'll use no-tillage direct seeding. Maize gets 18 kg N, 6 kg P, and 5 kg K per mu, with two irrigations if the weather stays dry. The cotton on my other 4 mu needs more pesticide attention—about 10 sprayings through the season for bollworm and aphids—but the returns have been decent. I'll rotary till both the cotton field and the wheat field, and target 500 kg per mu for cotton, 1000 kg for wheat, and 1200 kg for maize. These are yields I've achieved in good years, and I'd rather plan for success than hedge downward.
